subject: Proof of Customer-Controlled Storage & Deletion Timeline for Private Deployments
messages:

Cc: security@medtechpartners.com

Subject: Proof of customer-controlled storage + deletion timeline for Private deployment

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

We're getting close to the compliance review for our Private deployment and need a few concrete artifacts from Redwood to satisfy our auditors:

- Confirmation that customer-controlled storage (the S3 bucket in our AWS account) is the canonical store for user data and that Redwood will not retain independent copies beyond configured snapshots.
- Exact timeline and steps Redwood will follow to complete a tenant-erasure (what happens when we request a full wipe), and a sample of the deletion events/logs you can provide.
- Whether you can provide a signed attestation (PDF) confirming deletion and absence of replicas across Redwood-managed replicas/regions.

Can you point me to the expected turnaround time and the specific deliverables? We may need this for an external audit the week of Apr 10.

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
Head of Infrastructure
MedTech Partners
security@medtechpartners.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and attaching a short runbook that outlines evidence we can produce (residency-evidence-steps.pdf). I'll loop Karthik in for the low-level details and exact commands/artifacts.

Summary (short):
- Canonical store: If the Private deployment is configured with customer-controlled storage (S3 in your account or a mounted block store in your VPC), that store is the canonical tenant storage. Redwood does not retain an independent primary copy beyond what is configured for high-availability/replication.
- Erasure steps: Typical flow is (1) request received + verify tenant ID, (2) scheduling and preflight checks, (3) issue delete to object store / lifecycle policy, (4) verify object-level delete and snapshot absence, (5) generate evidence bundle (deletion events + checksums + audit log slices).
- Timeline: If tenant storage is in your account (customer-owned S3), automated deletion events and evidence extraction are usually available within 1–3 business days. If Redwood-managed replication exists (cross-region replicas we host), full evidence and signed attestation may take 3–7 business days while we validate replica teardown and finalize chain-of-custody.

What we need from you to proceed:
- Tenant ID and AWS account ID (or GCP project) for the bucket you want targeted.
- Confirmation whether you require a signed attestation (we can produce a draft attestation if helpful).
- Any special regulatory language you need included (HIPAA/HITRUST clauses, etc.).

Next steps: Karthik — can you add the technical details and sample artifacts we can attach back to MedTech (logs, command lines, CSV sample)?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com
\Attachment: residency-evidence-steps.pdf (attached)\

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@medtechpartners.com>, marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof of customer-controlled storage + deletion timeline for Private deployment

Hi Samantha — Karthik here (solutions architect). Below are technical details and the kinds of artifacts we can produce. I'm including inline examples of what we'll capture.

Overview of evidence & mechanics:
1) Canonical ownership
   - For customer-controlled storage (S3 in your account / bucket ownership confirmed), Redwood mounts/reads and writes only with the IAM role/credentials you provide. We do not create an additional independent primary copy in our accounts.

2) Deletion mechanics and events we capture
   - Object-level delete: We trigger a delete via the configured connector (S3 DeleteObject API). The object-level deletion event includes timestamp, object key prefix, and request id.
   - Snapshot/backups: If you have periodic snapshots managed by your lifecycle policy, we will validate and expire snapshots; if Redwood maintains any short-term snapshots for upgrade rollback (only when explicitly enabled), we will tear those down per the tenant-wipe flow.

3) Evidence artifacts we can deliver (examples):
   - deletion_events.csv (columns: timestamp, object_key, request_id, actor) — see attached erase-log-sample.csv
   - audit_log_slice.json (filtered entries from infra/audit logs showing the delete operation and verification steps)
   - snapshot_manifest.txt (checksums + snapshot ids)
   - signed attestation PDF (draft attached; Legal signs upon final verification)

4) Timeframes (typical):
   - Customer-owned, single-region S3: 1–3 business days for automated evidence bundle.
   - Redwood-managed cross-region replicas: 3–7 business days to ensure replicas are fully torn down and evidence validated.

5) Edge notes:
   - KV caches and ephemeral in-memory caches: these are cleared during the wipe operation, and we produce a record that cache flush commands were issued; these are not persisted long-term.
   - Cold backups: if your environment uses object-archive or deep backups that are customer-controlled, lifecycle deletion is handled in your account; if Redwood retained any archived copies due to a previously enabled retention override, we will enumerate and erase those as part of the process.

Example CLI (internal) we run for inventory and wipe verification:
   - redwoodctl inventory --tenant-id <TENANT_ID> --out delete_inventory.json
   - redwoodctl tenant wipe --tenant-id <TENANT_ID> --confirm --evidence-out evidence_bundle.tar.gz

Please review the attached erase-log-sample.csv (synthetic sample) and let us know the tenant ID and your preferred acceptance language for the attestation. If you need SOC2/HIPAA mapping, we can add that as an appendix.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com
\Attachment: erase-log-sample.csv (attached; sample lines)\

What we'll do once you confirm Tenant ID:

- Execute tenant wipe per the runbook and collect the evidence bundle (deletion_events.csv, snapshot_manifest.txt, audit_log_slice.json).

For your audit week (Apr 10), we can prioritize an accelerated path if you confirm tenant details by EOD Apr 4.
